context:
Goal: one word means one thing.
Problem (rule): a child repo that keeps its own version of a rule on purpose marks it with a comment. The brief used `override`, but GLOSSARY.md already uses 'override' for the word you type to let a refused act through.
Based on (read): the plan, part c; GLOSSARY.md.
Departs from: main has no child-exception marker — adds `<!-- exempt: <rule-id> reason: <text> -->`.

options.gain: 'Override' keeps its one meaning, your typed word.
options.label: Yes: use 'exempt' (recommended)
No: keep 'override'
options.lose: One word for two things; a session may mistake a repo comment for your override.

short: One-home Q2 of 5: name a child repo's exception 'exempt'?
title: One-home check, question 2 of 5: should a child repo mark a deliberate rule copy with the word 'exempt' instead of 'override'?
why: From plan PR #1106, at your request on 333.
